<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Laugh Tough" /></noinclude><section begin="par107" />hand, with the perf., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=22}}. As after {{GHGheb|text=אָז}}, so also after {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּטֶ֫רֶם}}, and {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} the imperf. may be used, according to the context, in the sense of our ''future'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=2|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=21}}; after {{GHGheb|text=עַד־}} e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=14}}. The imperf. is used in the sense of our ''present'' after {{GHGheb|text=טֶ֫רֶם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=30}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=7|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|d}}
2. Driver ({{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}<sup>3</sup>, p. 35 f.) rightly lays stress upon the inherent distinction between the {{GHGterm|participle}} as expressing ''mere'' duration, and the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} as expressing ''progressive'' duration (in the present, past, or future). Thus the words {{GHGheb|text=וְנָהָר יׂצֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=10}} represent the river of Paradise as going out of Eden in a continuous, uninterrupted stream, but {{GHGheb|text=יִפָּרֵד}}, which immediately follows, describes how the parting of its waters is always taking place afresh. In the same way {{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲלֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=6}} represents new mists as constantly arising, and {{GHGheb|text=יִמָלֵא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=4}} new clouds of smoke. Also those actions, &c., which might be regarded in themselves as single or even momentary, are, as it were, broken up by the imperfect into their component parts, and so pictured as gradually completing themselves. Hence {{GHGheb|text=תִּבְלָעֵ֫מוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=12}} (after a ''perf.'' as in verse 14) represents the Egyptians, in a vivid, poetic description, as being swallowed up one after another, and {{GHGheb|text=יַבְחֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=7}} the leading on by stages, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|e}}
(''b'') To express actions, &c., which were ''repeated'' in the past, either at fixed intervals or occasionally (the ''modus rei repetitae''), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=5}} ''thus did'' ({{GHGheb|text=יַֽעֲשֶׂה}}) ''Job continually'' (after each occasion of his sons’ festivities); 4:3 f., 22:6 f., 23:11, 29:7, 9, 12 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=6|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=29|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=42|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, 39 (''I used to bear'' the loss of it), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ff. ({{GHGheb|text=יִקַּח|translate=used to take}} every time), 40:36 ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=17}} f. 20 ff., 11:5, 9, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=14|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=21|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=9|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=18|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=27|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=5|verse=25}} (of tribute repeated year by year), 10:5, 13:33, 14:28, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=8|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=13|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=25|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=36|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=42|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=15.40|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=14}}; even in a negative dependent clause, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=18|verse=10}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|f}}
'''2.''' In the sphere of ''present time'', again

(''a'') To express actions, events, or states, which are ''continued'' for a shorter or longer time,<ref>It is not always possible to carry out with certainty the distinction between ''continued'' and ''repeated'' actions. Some of the examples given under ''f'' might equally be referred to ''g''.</ref> e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=מַה־תְּבַקֵּשׁ|translate=what seekest thou?}} 19:19 {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־אוּכַל|translate=I cannot}}; 24:50, 31:35, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=13}}. Other examples are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=11|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=2|verse=2}}, and in the prophetic formula {{GHGheb|text=יֹאמַר יְהֹוָה|translate=saith the Lord}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=11.18}}, &c., cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=1|hidebook=1}}. So especially to express facts known by experience, which occur at all times, and consequently hold good at any moment, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=20}} ''a wise son maketh a glad father''; hence especially frequent in Job and Proverbs. In an interrogative sentence, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=17}} ''is mortal man just before God?'' In a negative sentence, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=18}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|107|g}}
(''b'') To express actions, &c., which may be ''repeated'' at any time, including therefore the present, or are ''customarily'' repeated on a given occasion (cf. above, e), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=44}} ''as bees do'' (are accustomed to<section end="par107" /><noinclude>
